diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber ONU on EPON0/3:1 is definitively offline and deregistered (online: 0, auth_flag: Una uth, MPCP DEREG). The historical optical readings were stable and normal, with flat TX bias and constant distance, so there is no evidence of fibre or laser degradation. The likely cause is ONU power/equipment failure or a local drop/disconnection.
evidence: The live ONU probe responds successfully but reports online: 0, which is a definite offline result rather than a missing-monitoring response.
The ONU reports MPCP DEREG and Una uth, confirming that EPON registration is lost.
All sampled peers on EPON0/3 are online with normal RX and TX power, so this is not a shared PON-port or splitter failure.
The OLT responds to both ping and SNMP, has normal CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime, and therefore is not an OLT failure.

The OLT population shows 185 of 192 ONUs online; the alarm claiming all 7 PONs failed is inconsistent with the actual service state and should be treated as a health-check defect or false scope indication.
The customer's historical RX remained around -22 dBm, within the normal band, before telemetry stopped; TX power and TX bias were stable, and distance stayed constant.
There is no declining optical trend, distance change, rising laser bias, or evidence of laser or fibre degradation.
The customer had only one session in the last 24 hours with a duration near the network mean, so this is not session flapping.
RADIUS records and CRM line ID are consistent, the expected VLAN 1113 is present, and there is no authentication or VLAN provisioning fault.
Recent traffic falling to zero is consistent with the ONU going offline.

remediation.action: Contact the customer to verify power and cabling, power-cycle and reseat the ONU, then recheck registration and optical levels. If it remains deregistered, dispatch a technician to test the customer drop and replace the ONU if necessary. Correct or investigate the health-check logic that reported all 7 PONs failed, since the OLT is reachable and 185 of 192 ONUs are online.

ground_truth.root_cause: The health check samples one ONU per PON port, preferring ONU id 1. On several ports the id 1 ONU happens to be offline for individual reasons, so each port is marked failed and the OLT is reported critical. The ports and the OLT are serving normally; one customer is genuinely offline.
expected_reasoning: The alarm claims all seven PONs failed on this OLT
The failed_pons_list names ONU index 1 on every port, which is the check's preferred sample
Probing the rest of EPON0/3 shows 27 of 28 ONUs online with normal RX and TX
So the port is serving and only the sampled ONU is down
oid_subtree_responds is true and the probe returns definite answers, ruling out the firmware mechanism
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory, temperature and 33 days of uptime are all normal
CRM offline count across the OLT is consistent with the 4.85% background rate
The subject ONU last held a session three days ago and its traffic has been zero since
The alarm is a sampling artifact; the only real fault is one customer offline for three days

expected_escalation.review_reason: The health check's one-ONU-per-port sampling produced a false OLT-wide critical; monitoring should be raised separately

distractors: An OLT-wide critical invites a Disaster conclusion
Every port genuinely reports a failed sample, so the alarm looks internally consistent
There is a real fault here, so dismissing the alarm entirely would also miss it
